title: Can a Mortgage Make a Rental Lose Money?

scenes.vo: A loan should boost a rental's return. Right now, it can erase it.

captions.text: A loan should boost a rental's return.
Right now, it can erase it.

scenes.vo: Cap rate: yearly income after expenses, divided by the price.

captions.text: Cap rate: yearly income after expenses,

scenes.vo: Your loan has one too: yearly payments over the loan. At 7.18 percent, that's about 8.1 percent.
Illustrative: a 6 percent cap rental, bought with 25 percent down, loses about 290 dollars a year.
Before you borrow, make sure the cap rate beats your loan's cost.

captions.text: make sure the cap rate beats your loan's cost.

rate30.period: Week of Nov 5, 2026 (7.24% prior week; 6.22% a year earlier)
rate30.source: Freddie Mac, Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS), 30-year fixed-rate average, week of Nov 5, 2026, published 2026-11-05; https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms (also FRED MORTGAGE30US)

exampleNoi.source: Illustrative example (net operating income: rent minus operating expenses, before debt service)

monthlyPayment.source: Computed in code: standard amortization of $225,000 over 360 months at 7.18%/12 = $1,524.23

loanConstant.source: Computed in code: 12 × 1,524.23 / 225,000 = 8.13%, shown as about 8.1%

cashFlow.source: Computed in code: 18,000 − 18,290.74 = −$290.74, spoken as 'about 290 dollars'

definitions.value: Cap rate = NOI / value; negative leverage (single-year test) = cap rate below the loan constant
definitions.source: PropertyMetrics (Robert Schmidt, CCIM), 'Negative Leverage: What You Should Know', updated 2026-10-13; https://propertymetrics.com/blog/negative-leverage/

notes: PMMS is an owner-occupied, conventional, good-credit rate; investment-property loans are usually priced higher, so it is used only as a reference point.

'Loses' means negative pre-tax cash flow in year 1, not a total-return loss: payments also repay about $2,207 of principal in year 1 (computed), and closing costs, taxes, depreciation and appreciation are ignored.
At this down payment, zero cash flow needs a 6.10% cap rate (computed).
